rounds.response:
I’m in the big-blind (out of position) with 6♣ 4♦—one of the widest, lowest-equity holdings against any sane opening range—and the small-blind has already put in the full 20-chip raise. Under the 2-player blind structure that’s equivalent to an open to 2-BB.

Equity & Range Analysis  
• vs a typical paired SB jam-range (~top 50 % of hands, i.e. any queen+, any king+, any Ax, any pair ≥2, suited broadways, most suited connectors) my 6♣4♦ has ≈31–33 % raw equity.  
• Pot odds to call are (20 - 10) = 10 more to win 30, or 25 %—marginally profitable in chip-ev if villain would jam any two (which I can’t assume). However, accounting for reverse implied-odds when I make bottom pair vs villain’s overpairs and the fact I’m out of position for every later street, realized equity is well below 25 %.  
• Re-raising is pointless—6-4 offsuit has almost no playability post-flop and even 3-betting to 60 compounds positional disadvantage.  
• Folding preserves 990 chips; losing 10 more here drops stack to 980 with no edge. The opportunity cost of continuing is thus high relative to future hands and position.

Strategic Decision  
GT-optimal under 2-player deep-stack is to fold marginal, low-equity offsuit hands from the big-blind when facing aggression.
